meta.caption: 1,100 breast tumors from TCGA-BRCA (RNA-Seq V2 RSEM, cBioPortal), projected into PCA space over 20,219 genes. Patients are split into bottom (q25) and top (q75) quartiles of the selected gene's expression, and each patient's distance to its own group's centroid is measured across the top 50 principal components. At this cohort size roughly 84% of randomly chosen genes reach P < 0.05 on this metric, so each gene is also scored against an empirical null built from 200 random expressed genes: the z-score, not the p-value, is the quantity worth reading.
meta.method: PCA over the 20219 most variable genes; distance to quartile-group centroid across the top 50 PCs.

nullModel.note: Spread ratios from 200 randomly chosen expressed genes put through the identical procedure. At this cohort size most arbitrary genes reach nominal significance, so a gene's z-score against this null is the meaningful quantity, not its p-value.
